name: Master of Psychological Science
description: This two-year course builds on an undergraduate psychology base with advanced study of research design, assessment and the main theories of human behaviour. Students run their own research project under supervision and sit in on supervised practice sessions.

name: Master of Counselling
description: Learn to work with individuals and families through talk-based therapy. Classes combine case discussion, recorded role-plays and reflective journals, and the second year is spent largely in supervised placement. The course covers grief, trauma and relationship difficulties.

name: Diploma of Counselling
description: A one-year entry course in helping skills. Students practise listening, questioning and goal setting in small groups, and learn how to keep case notes and work within professional boundaries. A short placement in a community service ends the year.

name: Master of Organisational Psychology
description: Study how people behave at work and how organisations can be designed to suit them. Students learn to run staff surveys, analyse selection methods and design training, using real workplace problems as case projects. Supervised consulting placements fill the second year.

name: Master of Human Factors and Ergonomics
description: Covers how people interact with tools, workplaces and systems, and how to design them to cut error and strain. Students observe real tasks, build usability tests and write design recommendations. Lab sessions use simulators and eye-tracking equipment.

name: Diploma of Applied Psychology
description: A one-year introduction to how the mind works and how psychologists study it. Lectures are paired with tutorials on simple experiments, reading research papers and writing short reports. It suits students who want a foundation before degree study.

name: Master of Forensic Psychology
description: Examines psychology within the legal system, from offender assessment to witness memory and risk. Students write mock reports, study court case files and learn how to give evidence clearly. Placements are arranged with justice-related services.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: A two-year professional course in diagnosing and treating mental health conditions. Teaching moves between seminars on evidence-based therapies and supervised work with clients in the on-campus clinic. Students also complete a research thesis.

name: Master of Counselling and Psychotherapy
description: Prepares graduates for private and community counselling work. Students move from basic skills to longer-term psychotherapy approaches, practising on each other in class and then with clients under supervision. Reflection on one's own practice is assessed throughout.

name: Diploma of Community Services (Counselling)
description: A practical one-year course for people who want to support others in community settings. Learners practise interviews, crisis response and referral in simulated sessions. Time on placement puts those skills to work with a local support service.

name: Master of Organisational and Industrial Psychology
description: Applies psychological research to hiring, motivation, teamwork and wellbeing at work. Students work in small consulting teams to diagnose a real organisation's issues and present their recommendations. Statistics and psychometrics are taught through the projects.

name: Diploma of Human Factors in Aviation and Mining
description: This one-year course looks at human error and fatigue in high-risk industries. Students analyse incident reports, learn how to design safer procedures and practise interviewing workers about their tasks. Case studies come from flight decks, control rooms and mine sites.

name: Master of Neuropsychology
description: Focuses on how brain injury and disease change thinking and behaviour. Students learn to give and interpret cognitive tests, write assessment reports and plan rehabilitation with clients. Much of the teaching uses recorded case studies and supervised clinic sessions.

name: Diploma of Counselling
description: A hands-on year in the skills of counselling. Classes are small and built around role-play, feedback and short written reflections. Students finish with a placement in a community agency where they sit in on sessions with a supervisor.

name: Diploma of Mental Health
description: Prepares students for support roles in mental health services. They learn about common conditions, recovery-focused practice and how to work respectfully with clients and families. Practical sessions cover de-escalation and planning care with a person rather than for them.

name: Diploma of Alcohol and Other Drugs
description: Teaches how to support people affected by drug and alcohol use. Students practise brief interventions and motivational interviewing, and learn how services work together around a client. Placement hours are spent in a treatment or outreach service.

name: Diploma of Youth Work
description: A practical year about supporting young people through study, family and wellbeing challenges. Students learn how teenagers develop, how to run group activities and how to respond when a young person is at risk. Part of the course is spent in a youth service.

name: Diploma of Workplace Wellbeing and Safety Psychology
description: An introduction to how mental health and working conditions affect each other. Students learn to run wellbeing programs, spot stress and bullying risks and write simple policies. Assessment is based on workplace scenarios and short presentations.

name: Diploma of Applied Human Factors
description: Explains how people and equipment fit together on the job. Students measure workstations, observe tasks and suggest changes that reduce strain and mistakes. Most work is done in the workshop and on site visits.

name: Master of Psychology (Clinical)
description: A professional course that trains students to assess and treat anxiety, mood and personality conditions. Seminars are paired with weekly supervised client work and group case review. A research project is written up in the second year.

name: Master of Counselling
description: A course for people moving into counselling from other careers. It blends theory with plenty of skills practice, and students keep a reflective portfolio over two years. Placements in the second year are in schools, clinics or community services.

name: Diploma of Psychological Studies
description: A pathway year covering the core areas of psychology: how people learn, remember, develop and relate. Students practise reading studies, collecting simple data and writing in the style the discipline expects.

name: Master of Organisational Psychology
description: Teaches the psychology of hiring, leading and changing organisations. Students build selection tools, interpret engagement data and facilitate workshops. A placement with a working team lets them apply these skills under supervision.

name: Master of Human Factors and Interaction Design
description: Brings the study of human perception and decision-making to the design of software, devices and public spaces. Students interview users, build prototypes and test them in the lab, then explain what the results mean for the design. Teamwork is central.

name: Master of Health Psychology
description: Looks at how thoughts, habits and stress affect physical health and recovery. Students design behaviour-change programs, learn to counsel patients about long-term conditions and study chronic pain. Fieldwork takes place in health settings.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: A two-year professional course in clinical assessment and therapy. Students learn several treatment models and then practise them with clients in the university clinic under close supervision. A research thesis sits alongside the practice units.

name: Master of Applied Psychology
description: A broad course for graduates who want to use psychology in schools, services and workplaces. Students choose a focus and learn through case studies, role-play and a long project in the field. Assessments include reports and short oral presentations.

name: Diploma of Counselling and Wellbeing
description: An introduction to talk-based support. Students practise basic counselling skills with each other, study wellbeing and resilience, and complete a short placement in a support service. The course is a stepping stone into further study.

name: Master of Organisational Psychology and Leadership
description: Combines psychology of work with practical leadership development. Students analyse how teams form and break down, coach one another and run an assessment project inside a partner organisation. Each unit ends in a short consulting report.

name: Master of Human Factors Engineering
description: Teaches how to design systems that suit the people operating them. Students use simulators to study workload and attention, assess cockpits, control panels and screens, and write design recommendations backed by evidence. Projects are often done with outside partners.

name: Master of Sport and Performance Psychology
description: Looks at motivation, focus and pressure in athletes, performers and teams. Students learn mental skills training and practise coaching conversations. Fieldwork involves working with clubs or ensembles under the guidance of a supervisor.

name: Master of Psychology (Clinical)
description: Training in the assessment and treatment of mental health conditions across the lifespan. Students learn in small groups, observe sessions and then take their own clients under supervision. The second year includes rural and regional placements.

name: Master of Counselling
description: A practice-based course in individual and group counselling. Classes are small and stress self-awareness, with recorded practice sessions reviewed in supervision. Students spend part of the second year placed in a service and write a reflective case study.

name: Diploma of Psychology
description: A first-year-style course covering how people think, feel and act. Students learn to read research, run a small survey and write up findings. It is designed to lead into a psychology degree.

name: Master of Organisational Psychology
description: This course covers how to improve selection, training and morale in workplaces. Students analyse data from a real workplace, run interviews and present findings to staff. Smaller class sizes mean regular feedback from teaching staff.

name: Master of Human Factors in Health and Maritime Systems
description: Studies how people make decisions and avoid mistakes in hospitals, ships and other safety-critical places. Students review incident reports, model team communication and test checklists in simulated settings. A final project redesigns a real procedure.

name: Diploma of Child and Family Support
description: A year of study about children's development and how families cope with change. Students practise observing children, speaking with parents and recording what they see. They finish with time in a family support service.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: A two-year professional course that combines coursework in assessment and therapy with long supervised placements. Students learn a range of treatments and are expected to write detailed case formulations. A thesis rounds out the course.

name: Master of Counselling and Mental Health
description: Develops counselling skills alongside a solid grounding in mental health conditions and the services that treat them. Students practise in skills labs, discuss complex cases and take on supervised placement work. The program stresses ethical, reflective practice.

name: Diploma of Counselling
description: An entry-level course teaching the basics of listening and responding to people in distress. Students work in pairs and small groups, write short reflections and spend time with an agency. It can lead into a counselling master's degree.

name: Master of Organisational Psychology
description: Focuses on the evidence behind good people management. Students design a selection process, evaluate a training program and study how organisations change. Work placements give them practice in surveys, interviews and report writing.

name: Master of Human Factors and Safety Science
description: Explores why accidents happen and how systems can be designed to prevent them. Students study human behaviour in complex settings, analyse accidents with structured methods and propose changes. An industry placement supports the final project.

name: Master of Educational and Developmental Psychology
description: For students who want to work with children and young people in learning settings. They learn to assess learning difficulties, plan support and work with teachers and families. Supervised school placements form a large part of the second year.

name: Master of Psychology (Clinical)
description: A demanding two-year program that trains students to assess and treat a wide range of mental health conditions. Teaching includes small-group case seminars, supervised client work in the teaching clinic and a research thesis.

name: Master of Counselling
description: Teaches counselling as both a craft and a science. Students practise skills in videoed sessions, study major therapy models and learn to work with people from many backgrounds. The second year is mostly supervised placement.

name: Diploma of Psychological Science
description: A one-year foundation in the science of behaviour. Students are taught how psychological studies are designed, how to analyse simple data sets and how to present results. It is a pathway into degree-level psychology.

name: Master of Organisational Psychology
description: Covers the research and practice behind selection, leadership, teams and workplace change. Students complete consulting projects in groups, then a supervised placement where they apply what they have learned. Coursework includes psychometric testing.

name: Master of Human Factors
description: An applied study of how people perceive, decide and act within technical systems. Students run experiments on attention and fatigue, test vehicle and device interfaces and learn to turn findings into design advice. A research project completes the second year.

name: Master of Forensic Mental Health
description: Studies mental illness and offending, and how mental health professionals work with courts and corrections. Students read case material, practise risk assessment interviews and write reports. Placement work is supervised.

name: Master of Clinical Psychology
description: A two-year course in assessing and treating mental health problems, taught with a focus on regional communities. Students learn through case seminars, role-play and supervised placements. A research project is completed in the final year.

name: Master of Counselling
description: A practical course for people who want to counsel in schools, clinics or community services. Students build skills in short, focused sessions, learn about grief, relationships and stress, and reflect on their own practice with a supervisor.

name: Diploma of Counselling and Support Work
description: A one-year course in helping people through difficult times. Learners practise interviewing, plan support for clients and study how to look after their own wellbeing. A placement with a community organisation completes the year.

name: Master of Organisational Psychology
description: Teaches how to apply psychology to selection, development and workplace wellbeing, with attention to regional and smaller organisations. Projects use real staff data. Students finish with a supervised placement and a short research paper.

name: Diploma of Human Factors and Workplace Safety
description: A short course on how design and human limits affect safety at work. Students walk through workplaces, interview workers and learn to suggest simple, low-cost fixes. It leads into postgraduate study in the field.

name: Master of Human Factors and Usability
description: A fast one-year course for graduates who want to study how people use systems and products. Students run usability sessions, analyse errors and report on how designs could change. Most assessment is project work.

name: Master of Child and Adolescent Mental Health
description: Prepares graduates to support children and teenagers facing emotional and behavioural difficulties. Students learn about development, family dynamics and school-based programs, then practise play-based and talk-based approaches under supervision.
